## Defined types

### <a name="k8s_core--documents"></a>`k8s_core::documents`

Declares a `k8s_resource` for each object in a list, e.g. from
`k8s_core::yaml_documents` or `k8s_core::helm_template`.

#### Examples

##### Vendored manifests

```puppet
k8s_core::documents { 'cert-manager':
  documents => k8s_core::yaml_documents(file('profile/cert-manager.yaml')),
}
```

##### A vendored chart

```puppet
k8s_core::documents { 'ingress-nginx':
  namespace => 'ingress-nginx',
  documents => k8s_core::helm_template("${settings::environmentpath}/${server_facts['environment']}/charts/ingress-nginx",
    { 'controller' => { 'replicaCount' => 2 } }, { 'namespace' => 'ingress-nginx' }),
}
```

## Resource types

### <a name="k8s_collection_rule"></a>`k8s_collection_rule`

For controls like "every Namespace has a Pod Security level", where the set
of objects changes between runs. At apply time the rule lists objects of
`kind` (optionally limited by `namespace`, `label_selector` and
`field_selector`), drops the `exclude`d ones, keeps those matching every
`match` condition, and generates one child resource per object, so each
object appears as its own resource in the report:

* `action => patch`: a `k8s_patch` of `patch` onto each object.
* `action => report`: the same, but noop, so non-compliant objects are
  reported and nothing changes. Without `patch`, every matching object is
  reported as a violation (a noop `k8s_resource` absent).
* `action => delete`: each matching object is deleted. Objects declared
  by a `k8s_resource` in this catalog are never deleted.
* `action => create`: a `k8s_resource` built from `template` for each
  object, e.g. a default-deny NetworkPolicy in every Namespace. In
  `template`, `%{name}` and `%{namespace}` stand for the matched object's
  name and namespace. The generated objects carry the run's `managed_by`
  scope, so they enter its prune inventory: switching the rule off (or
  excluding a namespace) prunes them. With `action => report`, a
  `template` reports missing objects without creating them.

Children inherit the rule's tags, so a report ties every change back to
the rule (and, with the Compliance Engine, to its check and controls).

`match` conditions are hashes of `path` (a JSONPath like
`{.roleRef.name}` or `{.subjects[*].name}`), `op` and `value`. `op` is
one of `equals`, `not_equals`, `contains` (any value at the path equals
`value`), `present`, `absent`, `matches` and `not_matches` (regex).

#### Examples

##### Warn on restricted Pod Security in every namespace but kube-system

```puppet
k8s_collection_rule { 'pod-security-warn':
  api_version => 'v1',
  kind        => 'Namespace',
  exclude     => ['kube-system'],
  action      => 'patch',
  patch       => { 'metadata' => { 'labels' => { 'pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn' => 'restricted' } } },
}
```

##### Report bindings that grant cluster-admin to anonymous users

```puppet
k8s_collection_rule { 'no-anonymous-cluster-admin':
  api_version => 'rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1',
  kind        => 'ClusterRoleBinding',
  action      => 'report',
  match       => [
    { 'path' => '{.roleRef.name}', 'op' => 'equals', 'value' => 'cluster-admin' },
    { 'path' => '{.subjects[*].name}', 'op' => 'contains', 'value' => 'system:anonymous' },
  ],
}
```

### <a name="k8s_patch"></a>`k8s_patch`

Applies only the fields in `content` to an object someone else owns, with
server-side apply under its own field manager. Unlike `k8s_resource` it:

* never creates the object: a missing target is reported as not
  applicable, not as a failure;
* is never labelled or put in a prune inventory, so no prune deletes it;
* with `ensure => absent`, releases only its own fields (fields no other
  manager owns are removed; the object stays).

A conflict with another declarative owner (Helm, Argo CD, Flux, an
operator) fails and names that manager; imperative kubectl edits are
drift and are taken back (see `drift_managers`).

Several patches may target one object; the title is free-form.

#### Examples

##### Label a namespace for Pod Security admission

```puppet
k8s_patch { 'Namespace/team-a':
  api_version   => 'v1',
  field_manager => 'sicura',
  content       => { 'metadata' => { 'labels' => {
    'pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn' => 'restricted',
  } } },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `k8s_patch` type.

##### `content`

The fields to own, as a partial object body (no apiVersion, kind, or metadata name/namespace).

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

`present` applies the fields; `absent` releases them.

Default value: `present`

### <a name="k8s_prune"></a>`k8s_prune`

Declare one per reconciliation scope; the title is the scope, which is the
`managed_by` value of the `k8s_resource`s it covers. It runs after all of
them, and not at all if any of them failed.

After each run it records the scope's objects in the ConfigMap
`inventory-<scope>` in `inventory_namespace`. Candidates for deletion are
objects in the previous inventory that are not in this catalog. A
candidate is skipped when its live `openvox.voxpupuli.org/managed-by`
label no longer names this scope (someone adopted it) or it carries the
annotation `openvox.voxpupuli.org/prune: disabled`.

Safety rails:

* `protected_kinds` (Namespaces, PVCs, CRDs and CertificateAuthorities by
  default) are never pruned; remove them with `ensure => absent`.
* No more than `max_fraction` of the inventory is deleted in one run
  unless `allow_mass_prune` is set.
* `prune => dryrun` reports what would be deleted and keeps it in the
  inventory; `prune => false` only records the inventory.

Deletion order is custom resources, then built-in kinds, then Namespaces
and CRDs, with foreground propagation.

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet
k8s_prune { 'platform': prune => 'dryrun' }
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `k8s_prune` type.

##### `inventory`

Valid values: `current`, `stale`

Internal: `current` when nothing is left to prune or record. Do not set.

Default value: `current`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `k8s_prune` type.

* [`allow_mass_prune`](#-k8s_prune--allow_mass_prune)
* [`inventory_namespace`](#-k8s_prune--inventory_namespace)
* [`max_fraction`](#-k8s_prune--max_fraction)
* [`name`](#-k8s_prune--name)
* [`protected_kinds`](#-k8s_prune--protected_kinds)
* [`provider`](#-k8s_prune--provider)
* [`prune`](#-k8s_prune--prune)

Valid values: `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`

Lift the max_fraction limit for this run. Defaults to $K8S_CORE_ALLOW_MASS_PRUNE.

##### <a name="-k8s_prune--inventory_namespace"></a>`inventory_namespace`

Namespace of the inventory ConfigMap. Default `openvox-system`.

Default value: `openvox-system`

##### <a name="-k8s_prune--max_fraction"></a>`max_fraction`

Largest share of the previous inventory deleted in one run (at least one object). Default 0.2.

Default value: `0.2`

##### <a name="-k8s_prune--name"></a>`name`

namevar

##### <a name="-k8s_prune--protected_kinds"></a>`protected_kinds`

Kinds never pruned.

Default value: `%w[Namespace PersistentVolumeClaim CustomResourceDefinition CertificateAuthority]`

The specific backend to use for this `k8s_prune` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet will usually
discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

Valid values: `true`, `false`, `dryrun`

`true` deletes, `dryrun` reports, `false` only records the inventory. Default true.

Default value: `true`

### <a name="k8s_resource"></a>`k8s_resource`

The title is `Kind/namespace/name` for namespaced objects and `Kind/name`
for cluster-scoped ones. Alternatively give any title and set `kind`,
`namespace` and `resource_name` (the parameter shape of puppet-k8s's
`kubectl_apply`). One object may be declared only once, whatever its title.

`content` is the object body without `apiVersion`, `kind`, and
`metadata.name`/`metadata.namespace`. It is applied with server-side apply;
drift is detected by a server-side dry-run, so fields the API server
defaults never show as changes. Fields another field manager owns are a
conflict, reported with that manager's name, unless `force_conflicts`.

Every object is labelled `openvox.voxpupuli.org/managed-by` (see
`managed_by`) and annotated with its Puppet title, which is what
`k8s_prune` uses to decide what it may delete.

Namespaced objects autorequire their Namespace, and custom resources
autorequire their CustomResourceDefinition, when those are in the catalog.

#### Examples

##### A Deployment that must roll out before dependents run

```puppet
k8s_resource { 'Deployment/web/frontend':
  api_version => 'apps/v1',
  wait        => true,
  content     => {
    'spec' => {
      'replicas' => 2,
      'selector' => { 'matchLabels' => { 'app' => 'frontend' } },
      'template' => {
        'metadata' => { 'labels' => { 'app' => 'frontend' } },
        'spec'     => { 'containers' => [{ 'name' => 'web', 'image' => 'nginx:1.29' }] },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `k8s_resource` type.

##### `content`

The object body, without apiVersion, kind and metadata name/namespace.
`metadata.labels` and `metadata.annotations` may be included.

Default value: `{}`

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the object should exist.

Default value: `present`

### <a name="k8s_wait"></a>`k8s_wait`

Fails the resource when the condition is not met within `timeout`, so
everything that depends on it is skipped. Use it when the gate is
something other than the object you just applied; for that, prefer
`k8s_resource { ...: wait => true }`.

`condition` takes the forms `kubectl wait --for` accepts:

* `ready` (default): the built-in readiness rules of `k8s_resource`'s `wait`.
* `delete`: the object no longer exists. `exists`: it does.
* `condition=Available` or `condition=Available=False`, or just `Available`.
* `jsonpath={.status.phase}=Running`, or `jsonpath={.status.loadBalancer.ingress}`
  to wait for the path to have any value.

#### Examples

##### Wait for a Job created by an operator

```puppet
k8s_wait { 'Job/db/migrate-42':
  api_version => 'batch/v1',
  condition   => 'condition=Complete',
  timeout     => 900,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `k8s_wait` type.

##### `satisfied`

Valid values: `true`, `false`

Internal: whether the condition holds. Do not set.

Default value: `true`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `k8s_wait` type.

* [`condition`](#-k8s_wait--condition)
* [`interval`](#-k8s_wait--interval)
* [`name`](#-k8s_wait--name)
* [`provider`](#-k8s_wait--provider)
* [`timeout`](#-k8s_wait--timeout)

##### <a name="-k8s_wait--condition"></a>`condition`

What to wait for; see the type description. Default `ready`.

Default value: `ready`

##### <a name="-k8s_wait--interval"></a>`interval`

Seconds between checks. Default 2.

Default value: `2`

##### <a name="-k8s_wait--name"></a>`name`

namevar

The object reference, `Kind/namespace/name` or `Kind/name`, or any title with kind and resource_name set.

##### <a name="-k8s_wait--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `k8s_wait` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet will usually
discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

##### <a name="-k8s_wait--timeout"></a>`timeout`

Seconds to wait before failing. Default 300.

Default value: `300`

## Functions

### <a name="k8s_core--helm_template"></a>`k8s_core::helm_template`

Type: Ruby 4.x API

Runs `helm template` against a chart directory or packaged `.tgz` on the
compiling host, never a remote repository, so every object is in the
catalog (which is what makes pruning and reporting complete). Chart hooks
are rendered as ordinary objects; order them with relationships or
`k8s_wait` if they matter. Requires `helm` on the PATH of the compiler.

#### `k8s_core::helm_template(String[1] $chart, Optional[Hash] $values, Optional[Hash] $options)`

Runs `helm template` against a chart directory or packaged `.tgz` on the
compiling host, never a remote repository, so every object is in the
catalog (which is what makes pruning and reporting complete). Chart hooks
are rendered as ordinary objects; order them with relationships or
`k8s_wait` if they matter. Requires `helm` on the PATH of the compiler.

Returns: `Array[Hash]` The rendered objects.

##### `chart`

Data type: `String[1]`

Path to a chart directory or `.tgz`, e.g. `"${module_path}/charts/ingress-nginx"`.

##### `values`

Data type: `Optional[Hash]`

Chart values.

##### `options`

Data type: `Optional[Hash]`

`release_name` (default `release`), `namespace`,
`include_crds` (default true), `kube_version`, `api_versions` (Array),
`helm` (path to the binary).

### <a name="k8s_core--yaml_documents"></a>`k8s_core::yaml_documents`

Type: Ruby 4.x API

Empty documents are dropped and `kind: List` documents are expanded, so the
result is one hash per object, ready for `k8s_core::documents` or
`k8s_resource`. Only plain YAML types are allowed (no aliases or tags).

#### `k8s_core::yaml_documents(String $yaml)`

Empty documents are dropped and `kind: List` documents are expanded, so the
result is one hash per object, ready for `k8s_core::documents` or
`k8s_resource`. Only plain YAML types are allowed (no aliases or tags).

Returns: `Array[Hash]` The objects, in document order.

##### `yaml`

Data type: `String`

Multi-document YAML, e.g. from `file()` or `epp()`.

## Tasks

### <a name="drain"></a>`drain`

Cordons a node and evicts its pods, respecting PodDisruptionBudgets.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `node`

Data type: `String[1]`

Node name.

##### `timeout`

Data type: `Integer[1]`

Seconds to wait for evictions (PDBs may delay them).

##### `ignore_daemonsets`

Data type: `Boolean`

Leave DaemonSet pods in place (they would be recreated).

##### `delete_emptydir_data`

Data type: `Boolean`

Evict pods using emptyDir volumes, losing that data.

### <a name="rollout_restart"></a>`rollout_restart`

Restarts a Deployment, StatefulSet or DaemonSet and waits for the rollout.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `namespace`

Data type: `String[1]`

Namespace of the workload.

##### `workload`

Data type: `Pattern[/^(?i:deployment|statefulset|daemonset)\/.+$/]`

deployment/NAME, statefulset/NAME or daemonset/NAME.

##### `wait`

Data type: `Boolean`

Wait for the rollout to finish.

##### `timeout`

Data type: `Integer[1]`

Seconds to wait.

### <a name="run_job"></a>`run_job`

Runs a Kubernetes Job to completion and returns its logs and status, then deletes it.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `namespace`

Data type: `String[1]`

Namespace to run the Job in.

##### `image`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Container image. With from_cronjob, replaces every container's image.

##### `command`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

Command (with arguments) for a Job built from image.

##### `from_cronjob`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Create the Job from this CronJob's jobTemplate.

##### `env`

Data type: `Optional[Hash[String, String]]`

Environment variables added to every container.

##### `service_account`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

ServiceAccount for a Job built from image.

##### `name`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Job name prefix. Default: the CronJob name, or bolt-job.

##### `timeout`

Data type: `Integer[1]`

Seconds to wait for completion.

##### `keep`

Data type: `Boolean`

Keep the Job afterwards instead of deleting it.

### <a name="scale"></a>`scale`

Scales a workload. Refuses when another manager (such as the reconciler) owns spec.replicas, unless forced.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `namespace`

Data type: `String[1]`

Namespace of the workload.

##### `workload`

Data type: `Pattern[/^(?i:deployment|statefulset)\/.+$/]`

deployment/NAME or statefulset/NAME.

##### `replicas`

Data type: `Integer[0]`

Desired replicas.

##### `force`

Data type: `Boolean`

Scale even if another field manager owns spec.replicas; the owner will revert it on its next run.

##### `wait`

Data type: `Boolean`

Wait until the workload is ready.

##### `timeout`

Data type: `Integer[1]`

Seconds to wait.

### <a name="uncordon"></a>`uncordon`

Marks a node schedulable again.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `node`

Data type: `String[1]`

Node name.

### <a name="wait_node_ready"></a>`wait_node_ready`

Waits for a node to report Ready.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `node`

Data type: `String[1]`

Node name.

##### `timeout`

Data type: `Integer[1]`

Seconds to wait.
